subject: whether and how moderated mediation model to account for nesting data structure?

messages.author: 7047c480ee5ca957
messages.subject: whether and how moderated mediation model to account for nesting data structure?
parts:
We’re working on a moderated mediation model and want to make sure whether we need to account for the possible nesting data structure. In our study, participants were asked to imagine four different ages (1980s, 1990s, 2000s, 2010s), rated normal people from these four different ages on some attributes, and inferred their behavior. We collected responses from two countries. Therefore, we conducted a moderated mediation model where year was the continuous independent variable (for simplicity), rated attribute was the continuous mediator, inferred behavior was the continuous outcome, and nationality was the moderator. We fitted the following model:

model_1 <- "

mediator ~ c(a_country1,a_country2)*Year

            outcome ~ c(b_country1,b_country2)* mediator

outcome ~ c(c_country1,c_country2)*

 

moderating_a := a_country1 - a_country2

moderating_b := b_country1 - b_country2

moderating_c := c_country1 - c_country2

ab_country1 := a_country1*b_country1

ab_country2 := a_country2*b_country2

ab_diff := ab_country1 - ab_country2

"

## Estimate model

fit_1 <- sem(model_1, data=Data, group = "Country", fixed.x=T, se="bootstrap ")    

 

We’re wondering whether the independent variable (four different ages) should be considered as nested within subject and add random factors to account for this nesting structure. If so, we tried the following command to account for the nesting structure (“ResponseId” represents subject) and got a warning message:

fit_1 <- sem(individualistic_as_mediator_model_1, data=Data, group = "Country", fixed.x=T, se="robust.cluster", cluster = "ResponseId")

 

Warning: observed.information for ALL test statistics is set to h1.

 

Any help and suggestions would be appreciated!
